title: Guidance on Tax Exemption Applications Ensures Disability Rights Are Not Missed
summary: To safeguard the rights of persons with disabilities, New Taipei City Tax Bureau recently sent exclusive guidance notices for applying for exemption from vehicle license tax to two specific categories. Eligible individuals should apply early; after approval, they can enjoy limited tax exemptions from the application date. The bureau stated that the targets mainly include: first category, persons with disabilities without a driver's license or vehicle, their spouse or relatives within second degree of kinship sharing the same household, or vehicles owned by such relatives with registration address matching the person's household; second category, persons with disabilities who have a driver's license but no vehicle, their spouse or relatives within second degree of kinship sharing the same household who own a vehicle. The notice includes application case number and exclusive QR code.

title: Social care is for us all, and we all must fund it | Letters
summary:
Readers respond to Polly Toynbee’s article on the new prime minister’s commitment to a fair system
Polly Toynbee (Battles loom over social care, but this fight must be won. At last, we have a PM who believes that, 29 July) is right that reforming England’s broken social care system will require winning the “attention, hearts and minds” of a public that knows little about it. Yet one of the biggest barriers to reform is that social care itself remains widely misunderstood, and public debate often reinforces narrow assumptions about who uses it.
Social care is too often equated with care homes and dementia services for older people. While these are vital, they are one part of a wider system. Demand has grown fastest among working-age disabled adults who are largely missing from the public and political narrative. As such, the assertion by Polly Toynbee that “the old must pay for the old” is incorrect. Social care is relied on by people of all ages.

body:
The Tainan City Government continues to promote the Ministry of Interior's Old House Extension Functional Renewal Plan, accepting applications until September 11, 2026. Briefing sessions have been held and on-site advisory teams started July 15 to provide application consultations. The subsidy applies to apartments aged 30+ years, 4-6 floors, and low-rise legal detached houses, requiring a structural safety assessment first.
